page: Amazon Web Services c8id.48xlarge is a dedicated compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors running at up to 3.9 GHz across the x86_64 architecture, this instance supplies 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs alongside 480 MB of L3 cache. It provides 384 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 7 GHz, delivering a compute-to-memory ratio of 2 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture includes 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 75 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational and throughput capabilities. The platform achieves top-tier scores in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core operations such as Clang compilation and ray tracing. The underlying Xeon processor incorporates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX-Tile, AMX-INT8) and AVX-512 instruction sets, enabling top-tier prompt processing throughput across small, medium, and 70-billion-parameter language models directly on the CPU. Single-core execution falls into standard-to-strong tiers, confirming that aggregate multi-threaded parallelism is the primary operational strength.

Resource allocation is dense and tailored for throughput, integrating extensive local NVMe SSD storage directly onto the hypervisor host. This eliminates network storage latency for heavy disk-bound tasks. While this instance does not include discrete GPU hardware accelerators, its specialized matrix instructions provide high CPU-based inference capability without requiring GPU resources.

AWS c8id.48xlarge is suited for highly parallelized workloads including large-scale software compilation, distributed database operations, fast-access in-memory caches such as Redis, high-throughput static web serving, high-performance computing (HPC), and localized data processing pipelines requiring high local storage density.
description: Amazon Web Services c8id.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System, featuring a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 96 physical cores, 192 vCPUs, and 480 MB of L3 cache. It contains 384 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining a 2 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 11,400 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Without discrete GPUs, it utilizes Intel AMX and AVX-512 matrix acceleration to deliver top-tier multi-threaded processing, robust memory read bandwidth, and strong CPU-based LLM inference. The instance excels in parallel computing benchmarks such as code compilation, decompression, and database queries. Tradeoffs include standard single-core speeds compared to its massive multi-core throughput. It is suited for high-density compilation clusters, high-speed Redis caches, static content serving, and heavy disk-I/O processing pipelines.
